task.title: Stop the serve port-fallback integration test from silently disabling its main assertion
task.description:
TestRunServeFallsBackWhenDefaultAddressTaken (internal/cli/run_test.go:1770-1820) degrades to a no-op assertion on any machine that already has a board running on 127.0.0.1:7331 — which is exactly the machine profile the fallback feature targets.

The test binds 127.0.0.1:7331 itself as a blocker. If that bind fails it logs "default address already taken (...); relying on the existing occupant" (run_test.go:1781) and continues. But the guard at run_test.go:1818 reads:

    if blockerErr == nil && "127.0.0.1:"+port == defaultServeAddr {

so when an external process holds 7331, blockerErr != nil and the only assertion proving serve moved off the default never runs. The test still reports PASS.

Reproduced on this machine during the PR #25 review: a live workbook process (pid 32065) held 127.0.0.1:7331, and the test passed with the skip message logged and the port check never executed.

Failure scenario: the external occupant releases 7331 in the window between the blocker attempt and runServe binding. serve then binds 7331 itself, waitForHTTP succeeds against serve own board, and the test reports PASS having exercised no fallback whatsoever. It would report PASS identically with the feature reverted.

Suggested fix — either:
  (a) have the blocker occupy an address the test controls end to end and drive serve at it (the hermetic unit test TestOpenBoardListenerFallsBackWhenDefaultAddressTaken at run_test.go:1645 already uses this pattern with an OS-assigned port), or
  (b) t.Skip loudly when 7331 cannot be occupied, so the degraded run is visible as a skip rather than a false green.

Deferred from PR #25 (merged as 7e348da) as minor rather than blocking because coverage is not zero: the fallback logic itself is covered deterministically and machine-independently by the five TestOpenBoardListener* unit tests (run_test.go:1620-1740), which never touch 7331 and fail under a full revert. This integration test only adds runServe-level wiring coverage on top. Confirmed during review that the test does still fail under a full revert while the occupant is stable — the hole is the release-window race and the invisible skip, not total absence of coverage.
